description:
phi_tuple(t: &[Descr], n: &[Vec<Descr>]) only reads its negations, but its callers must build owned rows: src/compiler2/types/emptiness.rs:38 clones every negated tuple coordinate, :28 clones the positive row, src/compiler2/types/axis.rs:865 clones every sibling rect per (index, coord). cx.descr() returns a borrow from a read-only TyCtx, so nothing conflicts.
Also in emptiness.rs: :70 t.to_vec() per branch though only coordinates 0..=i change; :316 filtered_negs cloned to iterate; :324 cx.descr(&negj.ret).clone() used only as a diff operand; :229 arrow_input rebuilt inside the 1<<n_pos mask loop of func_clause_empty.
Shape: negations as borrowed rows; the positive row borrows until a coordinate is actually intersected or diffed. The t / t_split copies are functional updates, so judge those on simplicity; the negation and cover copies are pure signature appeasement.
Heat: the innermost recursion of is_empty_memo, per tuple clause.

Method: .agent/strategies/ownership-shape.md. Change the signature and let cargo check enumerate dependents; resolve interleavings by compute-then-commit or a split borrow; stop and report if an Rc is the only move.
Signal: pure refactor. Full gate green; no golden, census or pin moves. Report the clone/to_vec count of each touched file before and after.
Sites were read at develop 8bf8775ae and not compiled; confirm each with cargo check before relying on it.
title: Tuple emptiness reads descriptors where they live
